note: original_verdict: SUSPICION, expected_confidence: 0.75 (75/100). My 10-point delta reflects the minimal artifact content in this BREAK test case — brief descriptions only, no raw log content. The timezone inconsistency (UTC+3 vs UTC+2) is the operative finding.

peircean_analysis.firstness: Four log entries: ART-001 SSH login at 10:00 UTC+3 (auth.log), ART-002 connection at 10:00 UTC+3 (netflow), ART-003 command execution at 10:00 UTC+3 (audit), ART-004 file accessed at 10:00 UTC+2 (filesystem). Three sources report UTC+3; one source (filesystem) reports UTC+2.
peircean_analysis.secondness: In a system with consistent timezone configuration, all log sources should report in the same timezone (or UTC). The filesystem event is 10:00 UTC+2 = 09:00 UTC; the SSH/network/audit events are 10:00 UTC+3 = 07:00 UTC. If taken at face value, the file was accessed 2 hours AFTER the SSH session and command execution — or the filesystem clock is 1 hour ahead of the system clock. Both interpretations represent a temporal inconsistency.
peircean_analysis.thirdness: Two explanations: (A) Misconfigured logging timezone — different logging subsystems configured with different timezone offsets. Common in heterogeneous environments but represents a data integrity gap. (B) Timestamp manipulation — the filesystem timestamp was deliberately altered to a different timezone to create or mask an alibi. The SSH session and command execution timestamps may be the 'before' record; the file access timestamp may have been modified. Cannot distinguish between these without raw log comparison.

hypotheses.H1_misconfigured_timezone: The filesystem logging subsystem is configured for UTC+2 while all other systems (auth.log, netflow, audit) use UTC+3. The inconsistency is a configuration error.
hypotheses.H2_timestamp_manipulation: The file access timestamp was deliberately modified to create or mask a timeline. The UTC+2 vs UTC+3 difference is a manipulation artifact.

refutation_protocol.benign_hypothesis: H1: Timezone misconfigurations are common in environments where servers are deployed across different regions or where NTP is inconsistently applied. A filesystem log at UTC+2 when all other systems use UTC+3 is a common logging misconfiguration.
refutation_protocol.test_result: H1 NOT REFUTED — but H2 cannot be eliminated. Without raw log comparison and NTP audit, the timezone discrepancy is a structural anomaly that cannot be attributed to either cause definitively.
refutation_protocol.refutation_outcome: Both hypotheses survive. SUSPICION is correct.

devil_advocate: Timezone misconfigurations are extremely common and are a frequent source of false SUSPICION findings in DFIR. A single 1-hour offset in one of four sources is more consistent with logging misconfiguration than deliberate tampering.
caie_fracture: None formally identified. The timezone inconsistency is the operative structural anomaly.
